reason: Phenotype includes a broad neurodevelopmental/behavioral profile (ID, hypotonia, seizures, sleep disturbance, self-injury), plus multisystem findings (pneumothorax, hoarse voice, scoliosis, short stature/obesity, reflux, hearing loss) and some but not highly pathognomonic dysmorphology. This breadth favors keeping more phenotype-driven PCF candidates. Facial gestalt appears relatively nonspecific (broad/square face, synophrys, midface retrusion), so fewer GestaltMatcher results should suffice while still capturing plausible syndromic matches. Asymmetric allocation reduces review cost while maintaining expected true-disease coverage within the 20-result budget.
